designDirection.title: Kaydence Visual System v1 — the build-agent reference set
designDirection.summary: Five logo directions plus ten screen-family boards, each rendered for macOS, Windows, and Linux (30 OS-specific views) sharing one interface system. Generated with Codex from Plan of Attack v3, the Whisper-Ahead v2 interaction, and the monorepo PRD/ARCHITECTURE/ROADMAP, then adopted as the canonical UI/UX/visual source of truth for every screen built from P1 onward. Screen layout is fixed by the boards; the only free-tier per-OS variation is the selection accent (macOS aqua / Windows cobalt / Linux emerald).

designDirection.openDecision: Operator selects the winning logo (1 of 5), which locks as the app icon and public-site header across all three OS lanes and is captured in ADR-0012 (visual identity). Screen layout work may proceed with a placeholder mark in parallel — the winning logo drops into the same reserved slot without changing any layout.

osLanes.doNotVary: Information architecture, product states, prediction blue, merge gold.

osLanes.varies: Selections, active controls, Windows permission/injection copy.
osLanes.doNotVary: Layout, spacing, control density, feature hierarchy.

osLanes.varies: Selections, active controls, X11/Wayland and portal status cues.
osLanes.doNotVary: Shared module model, table structure, screen-family order.

invariants: One consistent left navigation across every screen: Dictate, Whisper-Ahead, Cleanup, Relay, Voiceprint, Conductor, Privacy, Dictionary, Analytics, Setup.
Card radius stays 8px; components are compact cards, tables, segmented controls, toggles, icon buttons, status badges, small charts, and native OS permission panels.
Prediction suggestions render blue in every theme; an accepted prediction pulses amber-gold for roughly 0.5s then settles to normal text.
Destructive Conductor actions always require an explicit confirm gate.
Never imply cloud sync for core features; Harbor is an optional hosted service only, and every Harbor service has a self-hostable path.
All controls keyboard-reachable, readable at high OS scaling, with no text overlap at narrow desktop widths.
Default, light, and dark modes exist for every OS; only the single free-tier accent differs by OS lane; premium theme expansion may add colors later without changing layout.

mission.name: Kaydence — Plan of Attack v3
mission.tagline: Speak anywhere. Ship clean text. Never leak, never lose, never lag.
mission.northStar: Own the machine, the voice, and the fleet: a local-first dictation platform whose flagship trio (Voiceprint, Relay, Conductor) no cloud incumbent can copy without abandoning its business model. Privacy line = transmission + persistence, not awareness (ADR-0006). Pay-once, three desktops, one behavior.

policies.notes: auto = merge own branch to main when all phase gates + standing gates are green with fresh evidence. No git remote configured, so 'PR' = local mission/ branch merged to main; GitHub 3-OS CI cannot run here (macOS-only host). Standing gates: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo test (3-OS via CI), npm run check, scripts/bench.sh --check (once it lands), scripts/audit-network.sh (network-adjacent changes). Critical decision paths (JUDGE-AUDITOR.md: non-negotiable reinterpretation, new dependency/network surface, platform code, model registry, cleanup/prediction/Relay-crypto prompt contracts) HALT for operator go + ADR.

Visual System v1 (designDirection) is the LOCKED UI/UX source of truth: build each screen to its screen-family board (assets/generated/kaydence-visual-pack/screens/kaydence-screen-family-NN.png). The only per-OS variation is the free-tier selection accent (macOS aqua / Windows cobalt / Linux emerald). The shared invariants — nav order, 8px card radius, prediction-blue, amber-gold merge pulse, destructive confirm gate, no cloud-sync copy on core screens — never vary; treat a change to them as a critical decision path that HALTS for operator go + ADR.

Every phase from P1 carries a screen-family fidelity gate: the phase's screens are design-reviewed against their boards (plus the keyboard/a11y checklist) before the phase closes. Logo choice is a separate operator decision (1 of 5) that locks via ADR-0012; screen layout may proceed with a placeholder mark until then.
Never weaken a non-negotiable to pass a gate — that is itself a blocking defect.
